title: Call-optioned hiring calendar + price sensitivity prototype
content:
Overview:
This is a working prototype (sheet-style) for a ‘call-optioned’ hiring cadence that ties contingent hires (contractors -> FTE conversion) to measurable pricing / usage triggers. Goal: preserve runway while allowing stepwise capacity expansion when revenue signals justify it.

Quick summary (top line):
- Current net burn (org-wide, ex-capex): $1.95M / month (Feb 2026 baseline).
- Base hiring plan (no calls exercised): +12 FTEs planned H2 2026 (engineering, SRE, CS), incremental run-rate +$1.02M / month fully ramped.
- Optioned plan: staggered contractor pool (40 contractors) with 6-month conversion windows. Exercising options adds headcount to FTEs only after reaching revenue/usage trigger bands.
- Pricing sensitivity scenarios model impact on revenue, gross margin, and runway under: -20% price compression, -5% (low), +10% uplift (price recovery).

Sheet layout (tabs described as sections):
1) HEADCOUNT LANE (tab: headcount_calendar) — table view
Columns: Month | Role | Status (vacant/offer/contractor/FTE) | Planned start | Cost/month (fully burdened) | Conversion-trigger | Notes
Sample rows:
Feb-2026 | Backend Eng | contractor (opt) | 2026-02-15 | $18,000 | usage > 12B tokens/mo OR route latency > 25ms degraded | 12 contractors pool, convert 1 per threshold
Mar-2026 | SRE | vacant | 2026-03-01 | $22,000 | sustained 95% infra utilization on dedicated pools for 6w | prioritize contractor->FTE
May-2026 | CS (Enterprise) | offer | 2026-05-10 | $13,500 | ARR motion: 3 contracts > $200k TCV in trailing 90d

2) COST-BRIDGE (tab: cost_bridge) — waterfall for monthly burn
Base burn Feb-2026: $1,945,000
+ Contractor pool provisioning (40 pax * avg $9.5k): +$380,000 (variable bucket)
+ Planned FTE ramp (12 FTEs phased): +$420,000 (phased; full run-rate +$1.02M after full ramp)
- Savings if deferred hires (3-month delay of tranche A): -$315,000 over quarter
= Projected burn (optioned, mid-case exercise): $2.28M / month at mid-point of ramp

3) PRICING SENSITIVITY (tab: pricing_scenarios) — simplified P&L snapshots
Assumptions (base): Monthly revenue = $4.2M; gross margin (pre-hc) = 38%; token growth = 8% MoM baseline; price per 1M tokens (effective blended) = $2.80
Elasticity assumptions (conservative): Price change -> demand shift
- -20% price (to $2.24): demand uplift +12% (more usage from price-sensitive customers); revenue net change = -9.6% (~$3.8M)
- -5% price (to $2.66): demand uplift +2% -> revenue -3.3% (~$4.06M)
- +10% price (to $3.08): demand fall -6% -> revenue +3.8% (~$4.36M)

Outputs (monthly snapshots):
Scenario | Rev | Gross margin | Monthly net burn | Runway (months, from $60M cash)
Base | $4.2M | 38% | $1.95M | 30.8
-20% Price | $3.8M | 36% (higher GPU mix) | $2.32M | 25.9
-5% Price | $4.06M | 37% | $2.07M | 28.9
+10% Price | $4.36M | 39.5% | $1.78M | 33.9

Interpretation notes:
- The optioned hiring plan is most valuable under the -20% price case where runway compresses; contractor-first stance buys ~1.5–2 months of runway relative to immediate FTE ramp.
- Under price uplift (+10%), exercising conversion options earlier (aggressive hiring) increases revenue capture (sales enablement) and maintains latency SLOs with minimal net burn delta.

4) TRIGGER LOGIC (tab: triggers) — hard/soft triggers and decision cadence
Trigger types: usage, revenue, infra utilization, SLA events, sales-qualified pipeline
- Usage triggers (quantitative): 3-day rolling avg tokens > 85% of reserved throughput for >10d -> start converting 2 contractors for backend optimizations.
- Revenue triggers (qualitative->quant): 90d trailing new ARR >= $500k across >=3 logos -> convert 1 AE to FTE per $250k increment.
- Infra triggers: sustained GPU utilization > 92% on Dedicated for two weeks and queue latency tail > 95th percentile threshold -> move SRE from contractor->FTE.
Decision cadence: Finance + Eng Ops review every 2 weeks; conversion authorizations require CFO + VP Eng signoff for >2 FTE conversions in one month.

5) SENSITIVITY ENGINE (tab: sensitivity_matrix) — grid outputs (sample)
Grid axes: price delta (-30%..+30%) vs token elasticity (low/moderate/high). Cells show: delta in monthly revenue, delta in gross margin, hires deferred possible, incremental runway months gained/lost.
Sample cell: price -15% / elasticity moderate -> revenue -7.1% -> runway down by ~3.1 months -> recommend defer 4 FTEs and expand contractor pool by +8.

6) RISK & MITIGATIONS (tab: risk_mitigations)
- Risk: customers degrade quality with quantization/optimizer changes -> churn. Mitigation: trial A/B on 5% of traffic; tie to rollback policy and financial hit-estimates.
- Risk: contractors leave before conversion window -> pool replenishment gap. Mitigation: two-week retention bonus for conversion candidates; 3-month lookahead hiring cadence.
- Risk: pricing moves trigger legal/contract churn for enterprise customers. Mitigation: grandfathering clause with timed opt-in for new price bands.

Open items / TODOs (working list):
- (FIN-478) Validate elasticity numbers with sales and product (Priya) — current assumptions are heuristics from prior market tests; need customer-level elasticity by segment.
- Build a lightweight dashboard in Looker for the 3-day rolling throughput trigger (SRE team owners: Marcus).
- Re-run model with GPU spot vs reserved mix sensitivity (infra owns).
- Confirm contractor burden rate calculation (currently using 25% burden); ask People Ops for updated employer costs by role.

Actionable decisions suggested for next 2 weeks:
1) Approve contractor pool deployment (40 pax) with month-to-month contracts and 2-week retention bonus on conversion.
2) Delay tranche A FTE hires (4 roles) by 8 weeks unless revenue triggers reach soft thresholds.
3) Build automated alerting (Looker + PagerDuty) for the three quantitative infra/usage triggers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on elasticity; if Sales surfaces stronger demand at lower prices we should re-evaluate trading off immediate revenue vs share.
- The optioned approach is design to smooth hiring cadence and give Finance optionality (hence the name). It is not a commitment to hire — conversion is conditional and requires cross-functional signoff.

Appendix (compact tables):
Headcount summary (current vs optioned vs committed):
- Current FTEs (core ops & eng): 248
- Contractor pool: current 18; optioned target 40
- Committed hires (offers accepted): 5 (start dates Mar–May 2026)
- Optioned / contingent hires (subject to triggers): 35

Unit economics snapshot (base):
- ARPU (monthly, blended across hosted/dedicated): $5,200 per active customer
- Blended cost per 1M tokens (infrastructure + licensing): $1.72
- Contribution margin (post infra, pre HC): 38%

Footnotes / references:
- Linked JIRA, confluence pages above.
- For scenarios: price elasticities borrowed from internal Q3 2024 price experiment (small business segment) scaled by enterprise weighting.
